plants_chloroplast_0001: Chloroplast and thylakoid chlorophyll are confirmed in Biology 2e 8.1. Nucleus, mitochondrion and Golgi have other roles; none is the plant photosynthetic organelle. RU organelle terms match EN singulars.
plants_cactus_spines_0001: Figure 30.35 specifically identifies prickly-pear spines as modified leaves and green stems as photosynthetic. The scope is this cactus, avoiding other kinds of thorns. Root, petal and stamen are distinct plant organs in both languages.
plants_coast_redwood_0001: Figure 30.31 identifies Sequoia sempervirens as the tallest tree species, not the greatest-volume giant sequoia. Douglas fir is corrected to pseudotsuga in Russian; all four options are different tree taxa. No changing individual-tree height record is asserted.
plants_flytrap_leaves_0001: Changed draft plural to one leaf after checking Kew: its two lobes belong to the same modified leaf. Root, flower and fruit do not form the trap. Kew confirms sensory hairs; the claim does not reproduce the textbook's misleading two-leaves wording.
plants_guard_cells_0001: Transport section confirms paired guard cells open/close stomata. Replaced source's membrane/cytoplasm/cellulose with other cell types, removing its category mismatch. RU 'Камера охраны' corrected to 'Замыкающие клетки'; both questions ask regulation, not generic passage.
plants_transpiration_0001: Xylem section defines water-vapor loss as transpiration and links evaporation to tension. Condensation is opposite phase change, fermentation a biochemical process, crystallization solid formation. RU/EN questions and explanations have equal scope.
plants_negative_gravitropism_0001: Gravity section explicitly distinguishes negative shoot gravitropism from positive root response. The stem's gravity direction is specified, not inferred from illumination. Phototropism answers describe another stimulus. Both languages preserve 'against gravity'.
plants_ethylene_0001: Ethylene section confirms volatile gas and fruit ripening, including neighboring fruit. Other named hormones are not gaseous; this qualifier resolves overlapping effects on fruit development. Names and explanation are equivalent RU/EN.
plants_phytochrome_0001: Red/far-red section explicitly names Pr/Pfr as phytochrome forms. Rewrote broad original flowering question to the distinctive photoreceptor forms so auxin/gibberellin involvement cannot create another answer. Phototropin, cryptochrome and chlorophyll do not have these forms.
plants_oxygen_source_0001: Photosystem II section confirms two H2O split for one diatomic O2. CO2 supplies carbon rather than released oxygen; H2O2 decomposition is not the specified photosynthetic source, and CO is not that substrate. Subscripts and compound names match RU/EN.
human_body_iris_0001: NEI identifies the iris as colored tissue controlling pupil size. Cornea is transparent, retina light-sensitive tissue and lens focusing tissue; all are eye structures. Source's Russian 'ирис/ученик' and unrelated cochlea distractor are corrected.
human_body_paired_kidneys_0001: NIDDK explicitly describes two kidneys on opposite sides of the spine. Liver, stomach and gallbladder are unpaired in typical anatomy. 'Typical/обычное строение' avoids claiming everyone has two kidneys; source's mistranslated 'пару А' removed.
human_body_bladder_0001: NIDDK states urine flows via ureters into the bladder for storage. Gallbladder stores bile; stomach and pancreas do not store urine. RU uses мочеточники, not мочеиспускательный канал, matching EN ureters.
human_body_heart_chambers_0001: NHLBI anatomy explicitly gives four chambers: two atria and two ventricles. Other counts are incompatible with specified normal human anatomy. Numerals identical in both locales; no physiological diagnosis or treatment advice.
human_body_alveoli_0001: NHLBI confirms air sacs at bronchiole ends and oxygen/CO2 exchange with surrounding capillaries. Changed original to ask for air sacs: capillaries also participate in exchange but are blood vessels, so cannot be second correct answer. Bronchi and bronchioles are tubes.
human_body_cochlea_0001: NIDCD steps 3–4 explicitly identify the fluid-filled snail-shaped cochlea and sensory hair cells. Eardrum, auditory tube and pinna are neither this inner-ear structure nor spiral fluid-filled sensory organ. Russian улитка and English cochlea refer to the same structure.
human_body_bile_producer_0001: NIDDK distinguishes liver producing bile from gallbladder storing it. Pancreas supplies pancreatic juice and stomach gastric juice. Both languages ask production, not storage; explanation keeps the distinction and fat digestion.
human_body_olfactory_location_0001: NIDCD locates olfactory sensory neurons in a small patch high inside the nose, with receptors sending signals to the brain. Other locations are not this odor receptor epithelium; question says odor-detecting neurons rather than all sensory neurons.
human_body_ileum_0001: NIDDK lists duodenum, jejunum and ileum as small intestine, versus cecum and colon as large intestine. Ileum last section confirmed. No alternate correct structure among distractors; Russian подвздошная is distinct from подвздошная кость/ilium.
human_body_nephron_0001: NIDDK explicitly names nephron as kidney filtering unit including glomerulus and tubule returning needed substances. Neuron, alveolus and osteon are structural units of other tissues. Both locales ask a unit, not the whole kidney or a single glomerulus.
mythology_olympus_0001: Met essay identifies Mount Olympus as mythic home and Zeus foremost. Replaced source's planet and hall options with mountains, so all options fit question class. Scope explicitly ancient Greek myth, not a factual claim that gods live there.
mythology_poseidon_0001: Met essay assigns sea to Poseidon, Underworld to Hades, sky to Zeus. Ares, Hephaistos and Apollo are other Greek gods with different domains in the same source. Neutral myth attribution and brothers in explanation match both locales.
mythology_artemis_0001: Met essay names Artemis patroness of hunting, Apollo's twin, bow and quiver. Aphrodite, Hera and Demeter are distinct goddesses; question is standard hunting patronage rather than any myth involving an animal. RU/EN names are conventional.
mythology_mjolnir_0001: Swedish History Museum names Mjölnir a hammer belonging to Thor in his struggle with giants. Spear, sword and bow are different weapon types. Question is about Norse mythology, not Marvel; transliteration Мьёльнир checked.
mythology_hermes_0001: Met explicitly identifies Hermes messenger with winged sandals and herald staff. Ares, Poseidon and Hephaistos are not the messenger deity among these options. Both question and explanation preserve this specific role without claiming there are no other messengers in Greek myth.
mythology_dionysos_0001: Met names Dionysos god of wine and theater. Neither Ares, Hades nor Hermes has this combined patronage. Wording uses 'associated' rather than an absolute exclusivity assertion; Dionysos/Дионис names match.
mythology_odin_ravens_0001: Swedish History Museum's Swedish text says 'två korpar, Hugin och Munin' fly around and report observations. Korpar is ravens, not eagles/falcons/owls. Avoided source's confusing name-etymology gloss; Russian вороны is the intended raven plural, not вороны/crows as a separate option.
mythology_anubis_0001: Egyptian Museum identifies black jackal head and cemeteries/embalming roles. Cat, falcon and crocodile correspond to other iconographic traditions, not this depiction. 'Commonly/обычно' allows varied forms and avoids absolute depiction claims.
mythology_athena_bird_0001: Met lists owl and olive sacred to Athena along with weaving/carpentry. Peacock, dove and swan are distinct symbolic birds, not the conventional Athena bird. Both localizations specify ancient Greek tradition and avoid broad zoological claims.
mythology_thoth_0001: Egyptian Museum calls Thoth patron of scribes, associated with writing and knowledge, ibis or baboon depiction. Sobek, Seth and Anubis are different deities. RU Тот corresponds to Thoth and писцы to scribes; no claim of a single invariant creation myth.
ancient_world_cuneiform_0001: Met derives cuneiform from Latin wedge and describes reed/wood stylus signs in clay. Replaced source's disputed absolute 'earliest writing' assertion with a specific etymological fact. Hieroglyphs, Phoenician script and Linear B have different names; no mixed script/medium options.
ancient_world_khufu_0001: Cairo museum Old Kingdom section assigns Great Pyramid to Khufu, in Fourth Dynasty context. Djoser is linked to Saqqara and Snefru to Meidum/Dahshur; Ramesses II is a later pharaoh. Khufu/Cheops aliases share one option; RU/EN refer to the same Great Pyramid.
ancient_world_vesuvius_0001: UNESCO confirms Vesuvius, Pompeii/Herculaneum, AD 79. Omitted contested day and month from the older page. Etna, Stromboli and Vulcano are different volcanoes. Explanation is an original factual summary, not copied UNESCO description.
ancient_world_papyrus_0001: Met describes papyrus from layered stalk pith dried under pressure. Skin is parchment, clay tablets and metal plates different writing media. All options answer 'made from what'; RU/EN preserve material rather than claiming papyrus is modern wood-pulp paper.
ancient_world_upper_egypt_0001: Cairo museum explicitly places Lower Egypt in Delta and Upper Egypt in south. Compass distractors distinct; no inversion from English blank to misleading Russian noun fragment. Both languages ask relative location, not altitude.
ancient_world_qin_emperor_0001: UNESCO description and criterion (vi) identify Qin Shi Huang's mausoleum/army and unification 221 BCE. Other named emperors belong to Han, Tang and Ming, not Qin. RU Цинь not Цин/Qing; both locales specify burial complex.
ancient_world_parthenon_deity_0001: Acropolis Museum identifies temple of Athena Parthenos and Pheidias's gold-and-ivory statue. Hera, Artemis and Aphrodite are different goddesses. Distinct from existing question asking city location and new owl attribute question; asks dedication of a specific monument.
ancient_world_rosetta_scholar_0001: Leipzig Rosetta Stone project names J.-F. Champollion and 1822. Carter, Schliemann and Evans worked on different archaeological subjects. Does not adopt page's imprecise 'trilingual' wording; comparing inscriptions is the supported explanation.
ancient_world_colosseum_opening_0001: Read complete opening paragraph via direct HTTPS when browser extractor timed out: Titus, 80 AD, 100 days. 44, 117 and 212 are not the opening games year. RU/EN explicitly AD/н. э.; imperial reign and festival scope fixed.
ancient_world_terracotta_discovery_0001: UNESCO gives discovery 1974 and describes warriors, horses and chariots. Other dates do not answer archaeological discovery: 1987 was inscription, not excavation discovery. Scope is army discovery, not when the already visible tomb mound became known. Both languages match.
